correctness.rationale: For each incident pair of distinct host edges, the centered squared score has one unique quadratic Rademacher monomial. All nonconstant monomials are orthogonal, yielding the variance. Exactly triangles in the line graph survive the cube moment: common-vertex stars have sign +1 and host cycles of length three have sign -1, with six orderings each. For d-regular hosts, shared-edge conditional binomial laws yield the exact complete histogram covariance, with two orthonormal binomial null modes. check.py independently validates 444 exact direct-enumeration assertions.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons and actual semantic searches identify feasible score and score-sequence enumeration, but no equal or stronger published formula for the third central moment of score dispersion on arbitrary fixed hosts together with the full regular-host histogram covariance projection. The closest previously recorded additive-score/cyclic-triangle cross-covariance is a different theorem. Classical quadratic-sign moment machinery underlies the proof, so a broader uninspected implication remains a priority risk; no novelty claim based solely on a failed search.
residual_risks: A general quadratic Rademacher-form cumulant identity, known trace formula or graphical-zonotope random-vertex law could yield these statements after specializing to signed line graphs; further specialist priority search is warranted.

value.rationale: Provides complete all-finite-simple-graph moment identities that recover an unknown natural invariant, the host triangle count, from an observable orientation-score statistic once host degrees are given. Strengthens the second-order masking effect to the ENTIRE histogram covariance matrix for any d-regular host, and distinguishes triangular-prism/K3,3 despite identical regular profiles. These are natural structural identification results beyond a single arbitrary finite example; known general sign-product expansion is acknowledged and not itself claimed as new.
